support.quote:
Although the percentage of Brass in the Brass-filled PTFE is not known, it 
can be determined from figures 1 and 2 that it is far less than 40%.

The Brass-filled PTFE samples discussed in this paper 
were evaluated using a Parr 6200 oxygen bomb calorimeter to determine the heat of combustion.

The scientists and 
engineers at the Materials Combustion Research Facility, in cooperation with seal suppliers, 
are currently testing a new formulation of polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) with Brass filler.

This Brass-filled PTFE is showing great promise as a seal and seat material for high-
pressure oxygen systems.

A similar metal filled fluorinated polymer, Salox-M®, was tested in 
comparison to Brass-filled PTFE to demonstrate the importance of the metal chosen and 
relative percentage of filler.

that Brass-filled PTFE is highly compatible with both LOX and GOX systems.

Two types of Algoflon®, another PTFE based material, were tested at the same conditions in 
order to compare them to the Brass-filled PTFE.
Algoflon® F7 is a PTFE virgin granular resin.

In comparison to the Brass-filled PTFE, a similar metal filled PTFE compound named 
Salox-M® uses Bronze filler in PTFE instead of Brass.

The mechanical impact results for Salox-M® impacted with 98, 
55, and 40 Joules at 10,000 psia in LOX are shown in Table 3.

Two types of Algoflon®, another PTFE based material, were tested at the same conditions in 
order to compare them to the Brass-filled PTFE.

Algoflon® E2 is a PTFE virgin granular resin 
which has been pre-sintered.

By comparison of the Brass-filled PTFE in Table 3 to TFE-Teflon® (PTFE) in 
Table 5, it can be seen that their performance in high pressure LOX systems is very similar at 98 
J and 0.062 inches in thickness.

The data 
listed in Table 6 indicate that the reactivity of TFE-Teflon® (PTFE) tested at 72 ft-lbs with a 
sample thickness of 0.062 inches increases by 25% as the pressure is increased from 60 psia to 
3,250 psia.
